findings.text: The first paragraph does the job. It says what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, so after a few lines a newcomer can say what the product is and why it matters.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The title and heading are about a different project, firstmate, not Athena. A newcomer arriving at Athena's home URL may think they are on the wrong page before they reach the lede.
findings.source:
/

Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: The next step is clear and is linked from the header. The page names prerequisites, a clone command, an install command and a first command to try, so a newcomer knows what to do.
findings.source: Next steps: "git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git", "./setup.sh", "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The lede promises a traceable commit with its cost and a verdict from a second model. Nothing on the page shows that output. The rest of the page shows a different skill, reading and explaining a codebase, so the main promise is never demonstrated.
findings.source: "get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict" vs. sections "States of a piece of work", "Transitions", "Claims and sources"

findings.text: Almost all of the page is detailed firstmate internals: yolo, secondmate, close-pending, exit 75, places-held. A newcomer interested in Athena has no reason to read it. It works as proof that every statement links to source lines, but nothing says how much of it to read before moving on.
findings.source: Sections "Start here" through "Claims and sources" (12 transition cards, 6 design cards, ~40 glossary terms, 45 claims)

findings.text: The header link speaks to an owner, not a visitor. A newcomer is told proposals are waiting for "your" decision, which does not apply to them and is not explained.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The page does not say what "predictions" are. Nor does it warn a first-time user, before they press Enter, that the command will commit to their repository or spend money on models.
findings.source: "It shows how it read the request and its predictions; press Enter to run it on your repository."

findings.text: "About this page" talks about internal repository layout, which means nothing to a newcomer. It also never says the page itself is generated by Athena, which would have helped make the point.
findings.source: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The "Limits of this study" section is open about what was not checked. That makes the study more credible, but it is buried far down the page.
findings.source: "f1 not run This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."
